events.title: ENIAC dedicated
events.summary: The U.S. Army dedicated ENIAC at the University of Pennsylvania on February 14, 1946 — the first general-purpose electronic digital computer.
events.about: ENIAC filled a room with 17,000 vacuum tubes and computed artillery trajectories thousands of times faster than human calculators. Programmers rewired panels and set switches to change programs — no stored program yet, but it proved electronic computation at scale was possible. Every server rack today traces lineage to machines like this.

narrative.whyChosen: ENIAC was the first large-scale electronic computer to operate as a programmable digital machine.
narrative.whyImportant: It demonstrated that computation could be automated electronically — the foundation of all later computers.
narrative.problemSolved: World War II ballistics tables took weeks of human calculation; the Army needed faster, repeatable numerical work.
